claims.exact_span: Every block, coinholders are diluted to fund ZCG. But ZCG is elected by ZCAP, a \~200-person panel whose membership is decided by the Zcash Foundation. You can join by posting on the forum regularly or by receiving a ZCG grant. 72 ZCAP members (36%) have received ZCG grants. ZCAP members are behind about 75% of all the money ZCG has paid out. The people who pay have no say, the people who get paid do. This needs to change.

claims.exact_span: In February 2026, coinholders voted 98.6% against Zcash Shielded Assets. ZCAP voted 70.4% for. In June, ZCG approved another $455K for ZSAs.
claims.paraphrase: Reports opposed ZSA polls and a subsequent $455K grant.

claims.exact_span: This isn’t about the people on ZCG. Any five people would face the same problem. The knowledge needed to allocate well is spread across thousands of users, builders and businesses. It shows up in what people actually choose to pay for, not in grant applications. F.A. Hayek called this the “Knowledge Problem”.
claims.paraphrase: Distributed market knowledge makes committees poor allocators.

claims.exact_span:
**Why the NSM**
The NSM holds ZEC in a reserve that later funds block rewards. No committee, no elections, no capture risk. The reserve starts paying out in February 2031, based on the latest governance vote.

claims.exact_span: * Donors, companies and crowdfunding can fill gaps, as they do in Linux, Bitcoin, etc.

The dev fund was never designed with money at these amounts in mind, so capping what orgs get is a very good idea. Maybe we should even get rid of the dev fund. It certainly causes governance headaches.

But there are several problems with putting it into the Network Sustainability Mechanism (NSM).

1. There’s a major risk the current put-it-in-the-nsm proposal becomes a dev-fund-in-waiting, where the reserve gets redirected later.
2. The NSM sets aside a chunk that pays miners starting around something like 2031. It’s a somewhat difficult-to-explain second issuance curve that seems to complicate both the economics and the story of Zcash. One of the best choices early Zcash ever made was, mostly, not messing with things beyond what was needed for fast privacy.
3. If the argument is “we shouldn’t just pay miners,” that is inconsistent with this mechanism: it still pays miners after additional steps. Ultimately the money mostly goes to miners for making blocks, unless of course it gets changed.

posts.neutral_rendition:
**I was thinking out loud. My own thoughts seemed irrational, but so did some of the arguments being made.**

I think it’s time to put all these debates aside. If we want to eliminate ZCG, let’s eliminate Coinholder as well. After all, projects like Linux and Bitcoin don’t have this kind of funding mechanism either.

We could even burn all the funds that have accumulated so far.

Let all block rewards go to miners instead. In other words, let them go to the BIG INVESTORS who put money into mining and producing coins. Would these investors later spend millions of dollars of their own capital to finance Zcash’s development?

I’m being completely serious.

Because abandoning ZCG and relying solely on Coinholder is, in my opinion, a completely irrational approach.

“The people who own the money should have a say in how it is spent.”

Yes, I agree with that. But the real question is: How responsibly are they exercising that right? We have no way of knowing how thoroughly these stakeholders research and evaluate the proposals they vote on.

You can criticize ZCG because its decisions are made by a five-member committee that evaluates proposals and gauges the community’s sentiment. But who questions Coinholder’s decisions? Why don’t we see the same critical attitude toward it?

Whenever I raise a question, the response I get is that the voting amount was too small.

So let’s look at a concrete example.

During the latest Coinholder voting round, a project that had been used by only 17 people over 75 days received 1.5 million votes. This happened in the context of the connections established by the people who sponsored the project and founded Zcash Labs.

Let me emphasize this again: We are talking about an application that was used by just 17 people over a period of 75 days. I’m not concerned with Peer becoming part of the main organization now. That wasn’t the case when the vote took place.

Meanwhile, ShieldedScan, which requested just $4,000, was rejected with 1.6 million votes.

Why?

I allege that this was because it lacked powerful connections. We say we want alternatives in the ecosystem, yet even a $4,000 alternative can be rejected by such an overwhelming margin.

**I think this is the real issue we should be discussing: Are Coinholder votes actually measuring the value of projects, or are they reflecting the connections and financial influence behind certain projects?**

And this is only the beginning. We may see 100 different proposals in the next round. How many Coinholders do you think will actually review and evaluate every single one of them? My concern is that the vast majority of proposals will be voted on without being properly examined.

I could present many more concrete arguments on this subject. But honestly, I’m not sure how productive that would be. This debate is exhausting, and it seems we’ll be having it all over again every two months.

So let’s be a little bold.

**Let’s eliminate both ZCG and the Coinholder funding mechanism entirely.**

Let’s see how Zcash development progresses through independent funding and private capital. Let’s expect the market and major investors to take responsibility for funding development.

We could then observe the consequences.

If we don’t trust the existing systems, why eliminate only one while treating the other as beyond question?

Consider these possible consequences of relying on private funding:

- A major investor dislikes your project and withdraws funding.
- A major investor refuses funding because you are from Russia.
- The US President opposes your country, sanctions follow, and funding is cut off.
- Financial markets weaken, VCs react, and funding disappears.
- The CCP provides more state funding than Germany; Chinese developers who disregard trademark law overtake your ideas while your funding ends.

I consider these risks inconsistent with a cryptocurrency intended to resist centralization. I worry this approach would make Zcash dependent on US Treasury policy and even more compliant than Ethereum. I also question why people accepting development controlled by capital oppose Crosslink: if they accept what I regard as proof-of-stake control of development, why oppose proof-of-stake control of mining?

posts.neutral_rendition:
Having worked in the bitcoin ecosystem for a bit now, I can echo that these funding models are sufficient and drive competition amongst hobbyists and not-for-profit efforts which improves their products/offerings.

I will also share that this means not everything gets funded. Bitcoin has many hobbyists who run community projects with no funding. This would likely mean a lot of community efforts, which have been historically funded in Zcash, would likely not receive grants and financial support as they are not core infrastructure.

This then turns to businesses, who hopefully are profitable, providing sponsorships to ecosystem projects in return for marketing coverage.

For example, I ran a research project that analyzed offchain transaction protocols. Grant orgs didn't want to fund it because it was simply research, no real impact on core protocol dev or direction. But, projects did sponsor me (I didn't take the money fwiw) for marketing services so I could continue writing research if I wanted to.

While this would be painful for a number of hobbyist, community, and/or non-engineering projects, I think that ZCG should finally be abolished and by proxy of this a number of projects that are funded today would no longer receive support.

Committees are not abolished in this model, to be clear. But a decentralization of committees and decision making is healthy(ish) and funding is probably solely directed to engineering efforts and for-profit endeavors.

Also, parties (directly or indirectly through professional affiliation) who are advocating for coinholder voting, whilst having previously benefited from the founders reward and/or personal token grants via the Dev Fund, should be met with extreme skepticism. I regard replacing so-called "socialist practices" with anarchocapitalist-themed oligarchies as equally centralizing and shortsighted; I also allege that it could be malicious.

Best of luck to you all.

claims.exact_span: Back in *September*, when heated discussions were flaring up about ZCG, it was clear that nobody---not even the ZCG panelists themselves, by all appearances---were comfortable with the funding stream handing their treasury tens of millions of dollars of capital every month, given the sudden and unexpected rise in the ZEC price. Nobody at any org in Zcash was comfortable with this situation. It presented a risk to the panelists, invited tumultuous and harmful discourse, and was completely unnecessary given the existing spending rate of the grant program.
claims.paraphrase: Reports September concern across organizations about rapid treasury growth, risk and unnecessary accumulation.

claims.exact_span: At the time, there was universal agreement (and legal confirmation) that ZCG could either stop receiving their funding stream and keep their existing treasury, or perhaps instead place a U.S. dollar cap on its treasury and return excess funds to the NSM. Various members of ZCG also appeared to agree with this. With NU7 upcoming, and a follow-up network upgrade several months away (in early 2027, most likely) it was important not just to do it quickly but also to get ZCG's consent, since they appeared to agree with it as well, and it was in their own interests, and it was in the Zcash community's interests. (Delays only allow ZCG's treasury to accumulate more funds, which would make the problem worse for everyone.)
claims.paraphrase: Claims universal and legally confirmed agreement on stopping inflows or a dollar cap, with urgency around NU7 and early-2027 timing.

claims.exact_span: ZCG voted on the most limited version of this deal: voluntarily asking for their funding stream to be sent to a lockbox identical to the Coinholder grants lockbox, still earmarked for them, but placed out of their reach without explicit one-time payouts during network upgrades.
claims.paraphrase: Says ZCG considered moving inflows to an earmarked lockbox released only at upgrades.

claims.exact_span: **They voted no.**
claims.paraphrase: Reports rejection of that proposal.

claims.exact_span: I heard two objections: one, that they felt pressured to do it before NU7 and couldn't make an informed decision in time, and two, that they desired a public community discussion and debate about the future of the grants program rather than a "backroom deal." I think the latter characterization is absurd; this was about ZCG voluntarily asking to have their funds placed in a lockbox just as the Coinholder grants funding currently is. It was not even about sending the funds to the NSM at the time.
claims.paraphrase: Reports time-pressure and public-discussion objections; disputes calling the limited lockbox option a backroom deal.

claims.exact_span: But fair enough! Due to the nature of the discussions on social media and here on the forum, @GGuy told me that ZCG would deliberate and start a discussion in the community about what _they_ thought should be done with the out-of-control treasury from their perspective. Sounds great! This would allow ZCG to seed the discussion positively, and avoid needless accusations of bad faith and malice on the part of people who honestly disagreed with the ZCG program but were afraid to begin community discussions because they feared being labeled biased or having their objections disregarded and dismissed for ulterior motives.
claims.paraphrase: Reports GGuy promised a ZCG-led community discussion that could avoid motive accusations.

claims.exact_span: We depended on ZCG to do the right thing, for themselves, for Zcash, and for their own grants program, and they had all of October to do it. **Instead, they sat on their hands and said nothing.** They needlessly forced their opponents to advocate for something they claimed to agree with, and be subject to this predictable backlash.

claims.exact_span: Now, one of the members (@artkor) has the audacity to characterize this as campaign against them when they were given every bit of leverage and every chance to decide for themselves what to advocate for the benefit of Zcash. For an entire month.

posts.neutral_rendition:
Back in *September*, when heated discussions were flaring up about ZCG, it was clear that nobody---not even the ZCG panelists themselves, by all appearances---were comfortable with the funding stream handing their treasury tens of millions of dollars of capital every month, given the sudden and unexpected rise in the ZEC price. Nobody at any org in Zcash was comfortable with this situation. It presented a risk to the panelists, invited tumultuous and harmful discourse, and was completely unnecessary given the existing spending rate of the grant program.

At the time, there was universal agreement (and legal confirmation) that ZCG could either stop receiving their funding stream and keep their existing treasury, or perhaps instead place a U.S. dollar cap on its treasury and return excess funds to the NSM. Various members of ZCG also appeared to agree with this. With NU7 upcoming, and a follow-up network upgrade several months away (in early 2027, most likely) it was important not just to do it quickly but also to get ZCG's consent, since they appeared to agree with it as well, and it was in their own interests, and it was in the Zcash community's interests. (Delays only allow ZCG's treasury to accumulate more funds, which would make the problem worse for everyone.)

ZCG voted on the most limited version of this deal: voluntarily asking for their funding stream to be sent to a lockbox identical to the Coinholder grants lockbox, still earmarked for them, but placed out of their reach without explicit one-time payouts during network upgrades.

**They voted no.**

I heard two objections: one, that they felt pressured to do it before NU7 and couldn't make an informed decision in time, and two, that they desired a public community discussion and debate about the future of the grants program rather than a "backroom deal." I strongly reject the latter characterization; this was about ZCG voluntarily asking to have their funds placed in a lockbox just as the Coinholder grants funding currently is. It was not even about sending the funds to the NSM at the time.

But fair enough! Due to the nature of the discussions on social media and here on the forum, @GGuy told me that ZCG would deliberate and start a discussion in the community about what _they_ thought should be done with the out-of-control treasury from their perspective. Sounds great! This would allow ZCG to seed the discussion positively, and avoid needless accusations of bad faith and malice on the part of people who honestly disagreed with the ZCG program but were afraid to begin community discussions because they feared being labeled biased or having their objections disregarded and dismissed for ulterior motives.

We depended on ZCG to do the right thing, for themselves, for Zcash, and for their own grants program, and they had all of October to do it. **Instead, I contend that they did not act or communicate publicly.** They needlessly forced their opponents to advocate for something they claimed to agree with, and be subject to this predictable backlash.

Now, one of the members (@artkor) characterizes this as a campaign against them, which I strongly object to, when they were given every bit of leverage and every chance to decide for themselves what to advocate for the benefit of Zcash. For an entire month.

IMO, this experience caused me to lose all faith in ZCG. I believe that, at best, they are paralyzed by indecision and committee dysfunction. I am disappointed and allege that they misled me and others about their intention to communicate publicly. I have no reason to believe any of them are malicious, so I won't engage in that kind of speculation, but we will not be given the same benefit of the doubt. And we have ZCG to thank for it.

I regard their leadership as poor and responsible for this situation, and I allege that some now seek to present themselves as victims. I am now convinced ZCG is, at best, ineffective and must be removed from the protocol.

The world isn’t using Zcash yet.

Our work is not done.

Now that we have significant budgets, it’s the time to deploy, not to retreat.

We should be aggressively scaling up our marketing spend, while bringing experienced nonprofit leadership into the ZCG organization to manage the larger treasury with mature oversight.

**The Zcash ecosystem was desperate for funding for years.**

Now that we finally have it, it’s shocking that anyone would want to throw it away.

Scale. Go to market. Set an annual budget and use it.

Polkadot has $140 million in treasury and spends $40 million per year. We've never had the opportunity to really get Zcash out into the world on a big scale. Why not try something new, now that we have capital?

**I am firmly opposed to the notion that private investors will consistently fund Zcash projects.** They won't, not at the scale that a foundation can. Builders will relinquish equity in most cases. I believe access to Zcash-aligned investors is difficult unless you are an insider. Zcash is still a very small investor pond. One year of success doesn't mean we're golden forever.

We don't need to win Bitcoiners over. The world isn't using Bitcoin. Crypto has not "eaten the world" yet. Our funding stream is our secret weapon. We do things our way. It allowed us to survive.

I believe Bitcoin has failed to achieve Satoshi's goals. Practically nobody uses it for payments. The chain has no privacy. Its value was captured by Wall Street. I oppose allowing a small group of massive coinholders to cancel community grants; I allege that doing so would further centralize Zcash for their own mining/NSM benefit.

Sure, Bitcoin companies exist, are prosperous, and some donate. **Zcash companies barely even exist yet.** Bitcoin's market cap is $1.62T today. Zcash is at 1.3% of that. Our ecosystem doesn't have enough successful companies yet for us to completely rely on crowdfunding. Name one Zcash business success story.

Our work is not done.

**Removing community funding is anti-competitive.** Some of the same organizations who relied on grants for years are now opposing community funding, now that they are fine financially. I strongly object to that.

Zcash finally made it to the big leagues. Hopefully we're not too encumbered by indecisive governance to capture our moment.
